requirements.description: The system must allow the customer to access their account via login and password.
The system must create a usage session after successful authentication.
The system must allow the customer to close their session through logout.
The system must require an active session to access restricted areas, such as customer profile and reservations.
The system must allow searching for flights by informing the origin airport, destination airport and travel date.
The system must allow one-way or round-trip travel searches.
The system must display the flight options found for each leg of the trip.
The system must display, for each flight found, information on departure time, arrival time and reference values ​​for the classes displayed to the customer.
The system must work with a set of previously registered airports.
The system must allow an authenticated customer to book an outbound flight.
The system must allow an authenticated customer to book round-trip flights in the same operation.
The system must generate an identifier for each reservation created.
The system must record the date on which the reservation was made.
The system must inform the customer of the identifier of the reservation created after completing the operation.
The system must allow the customer to consult their existing reservations.
The system must present the customer with a list of reservations already made.
The system must allow canceling a selected reservation.
After cancellation, the reservation should no longer appear as active in the customer's listing.
The system must allow the customer to consult their own profile.
The system must display the customer's contact details in the profile, including telephone number, telephone type and address.
The system must allow updating the customer's contact details and address.
The system must require the customer's current password to confirm changes to the profile.
The system must prevent a client from consulting or changing another client's profile.
The system must display to the customer their status in the loyalty program.
The system must display the number of miles accumulated during the year.
The system must display the total number of miles accumulated.
Loyalty information should be presented to the customer as query data, not as edit fields in the main interface flow.
The system must allow initial loading or reloading of the application database.
The loading process must allow defining the number of example clients to be generated.
The base payload must recreate key operation data, including flights, customers, sessions, and test bookings.
The system must provide summary operating information, such as number of customers, sessions, flights, segments, reservations and registered airports.
The application must restrict private functionalities to authenticated clients.
The client session must have limited validity and automatically expire after the configured period.
Logout should invalidate the session in use immediately.
Customer personal data must be protected against undue access by other customers.
The application must support a high volume of calls and queries, especially in the authentication, flight search and reservation flows.
Flight queries should prioritize quick responses, as they represent a recurring flow in the customer journey.
The solution must be suitable for growth in usage without relying on manual fulfillment for core self-service operations.
The application must be able to run in different environments, including local infrastructure, public cloud and hybrid scenarios.
The solution must keep customer, flight, session and reservation data persisted between application requests.
Each session and each reservation must have a unique identification.
Reservation and cancellation operations must maintain sufficient consistency to correctly reflect the current state of the customer's reservations.
The application must record minimum data for monitoring operations, such as reservation date and count of operational records.
Navigation should favor self-service, allowing the customer to search for flights, manage reservations and update their profile without human intermediation.
The system must present times, dates and values ​​in a way that is legible to the customer.
The main journeys must be accessible via a simple web interface, with clear separation between flight search, reservations, profile and support.
The environment must offer a simple means of preparing and checking the database for testing, demonstrations or operational restart.
The system must provide basic operating indicators to monitor the environment without requiring direct consultation of the database.
The flow called `Check-in` in the interface, in practice, works as querying and canceling reservations; A complete passenger check-in process was not identified in this repository.

There is a `Support` interface with the appearance of a real-time chat, but the corresponding backend was not found in the analyzed code. Therefore, this item was not treated above as a consolidated functional requirement.
No public registration flow for new customers was identified. Customer accounts are generated by administrative data loading routine.
No payment flow, seat choice or formal fare class selection was identified at the time of booking; the system displays prices, but the reservation observed in the code is simplified.
